title: The two early years behind San Francisco’s film rebate return

beats.text: Which return did San Francisco get from its film rebates? This is an investigative lead.

visual.sub: The 2018 report used two different ways to summarize five years

beats.text: An early study’s five-year table gave a multiplier of $6.84.

visual.label: The 2018 report used two different ways to summarize five years

beats.text: The $6.84 figure averages five yearly ratios.
Two early years account for 44.49% of reported local spending.

visual.kicker: Two early fiscal years account for almost half of the longer series

beats.text: They used just 11.39% of the rebates.

visual.kicker: Two early fiscal years account for almost half of the longer series

beats.text: In the five years through 2025, spending came to $4.75 per rebate dollar.

visual.label: Two early fiscal years account for almost half of the longer series

beats.text: In February 2026, a new law raised the cap to $1 million per production.

visual.kicker: The February 2026 ordinance changed what could be rebated

beats.text: The legislative cost model applied new rules to the same five historical years.

visual.kicker: The February 2026 ordinance changed what could be rebated

beats.text: Film SF counted wages and spending at local businesses across 48 productions.

visual.kicker: The headline $12.50 can be reproduced from the later annual report

beats.text: The later totals support its headline of about $12.50 per rebate dollar.

visual.label: The headline $12.50 can be reproduced from the later annual report

beats.text: How much of that activity would have happened without rebates? The records leave that open.
A lead is a question, not an accusation.
